title: ICAO Annex 9 §§3.44-3.45 — Improper Removal Procedures and Failure to Provide Written Notice
allegation_summary: The forcible removal of a passenger from LATAM flight LA8159 at Santiago Airport violated ICAO Annex 9 facilitation standards and the Chicago Convention. ICAO Annex 9 §§3.44-3.45 requires contracting states to ensure that passengers denied boarding receive written notice of the grounds and procedures. Chile is a contracting party to the Chicago Convention (Art. 37 — uniformity obligation, Art. 38 — notification of divergences) and the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (Art. 26 — pacta sunt servanda, Art. 27 — internal law no defence). No written notice was provided; no divergence from ICAO standards was notified to the Council. The removal violated international treaty obligations binding on Chile.

articles.article_name: Chicago Convention, Art. 37 — Adoption of International Standards
articles.article_text: Each contracting State undertakes to collaborate in securing the highest practicable degree of uniformity in regulations, standards, procedures, and organization in relation to aircraft, personnel, airways and auxiliary services in all matters in which such uniformity will facilitate and improve air navigation.
articles.applicability_rationale: Art. 37 is an aspirational uniformity provision. While it provides the treaty basis for ICAO SARPs, the direct violation is of the Annex 9 Standards themselves, not of the collaboration obligation.

articles.article_name: Chicago Convention, Art. 38 — Departures from International Standards
articles.article_text: Any State which finds it impracticable to comply in all respects with any such international standard or procedure, or to bring its own regulations or practices into full accord with any international standard or procedure after amendment of the latter, or which deems it necessary to adopt regulations or practices differing in any particular respect from those established by an international standard, shall give immediate notification to the International Civil Aviation Organization of the differences between its own practice and that established by the international standard.
articles.applicability_rationale: Chicago Art. 38 (notification of differences) is a State→ICAO duty; individuals cannot invoke it as a per-incident violation. Reclassified supporting; the per-incident violation lives at the Annex 9 SARP level. | legacy paraphrase: Any State which finds it impracticable to comply in all respects with any such international standard or procedure shall give immediate notification to ICAO of the differences between its own practice and that established by the international standard.

articles.article_text: Every treaty in force is binding upon the parties to it and must be performed by them in good faith (pacta sunt servanda).
articles.applicability_rationale: VCLT Arts. 26-27 are general treaty-performance principles, not norms directly violated by a specific removal. They provide the legal framework for why ICAO Annex 9 compliance is binding on Chile (via Chicago Convention), but the direct violation is of the Annex 9 Standards themselves.

articles.article_name: VCLT, Art. 27 — Internal Law and Observance of Treaties
articles.article_text: A party may not invoke the provisions of its internal law as justification for its failure to perform a treaty.
